articles.title: 'Put egos aside': Heinrich Klaasen keen to tap into Gulf Giants' wealth of T20 experience in ILT20 title bid
articles.summary: Dubai: Heinrich Klaasen has played 311 T20 matches across his 15-year career and led a team in just 48 matches. That's just 15.43% of his career.
articles.body: Dubai: Heinrich Klaasen has played 311 T20 matches across his 15-year career and led a team in just 48 matches. That's just 15.43% of his career. He's held captaincy duties for South Africa, South Africa A, the Northerns, the Titans, the Spartans and the Seattle Orcas. A year on from that stint in Major League Cricket (MLC) in the USA, the South African has been given the armband by the Gulf Giants in the fifth season of the ILT20.Curiously, in the Giants squad, David Miller has more T20 captaincy experience. Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Liam Livingstone, Azmatullah Omarzai and Curtis Campher have also captained teams across the regional and franchise T20 circuit. Instead of being bogged down by the presence of so many experienced heads in the squad, Klaasen wants to make all their experience count."It's a new tournament for me, new conditions that I'm not used to, but we've got so much experience in our team that I will definitely rely on a lot of our players and a lot of local boys that have got heaps of experience. I'm looking forward to the challenge and we've got an incredible squad and a very talented squad. I can't wait for the full team to arrive so we can have good chats and find our basis of how we want to do things," said Klaasen during an interaction with select media ahead of ILT20 Season 5, which begins on November 21.The 35-year-old has learned from many skippers along the way. Albie Morkel made the biggest impact, teaching him the art of making subtle field changes while still being aggressive. Henry Davids imparted the skill of forming a bond with a player to get the best out of them. Faf du Plessis, at the international level, brought different things, especially technical thinking on the field.I need to be free enough to still play the aggressive brand of cricket I normally play, or the normal way I play."I was always just shouting at everyone and trying to get the best out of them and realised quickly that the new generation of cricket doesn't work like that," explained Klaasen with a chuckle.Besides his sense of humour, Klaasen also brings the humility needed in a team sport."You will never be old enough and experienced enough to learn all the trades of cricket. That's why I've got heaps of experience in my team that I will rely on. I see the cricket game in a certain direction or a certain way, and other guys see the game differently as well. So it's very important for me to put egos aside and tap into the cricket experience that is in the group and the experience of these conditions and the knowledge of the opposition, so I can use it to my ability," he continued.Klaasen also brings a lot of firepower to the side. The middle-order batter has scored more than 7,000 runs in T20s while piling up 1,000 runs in 58 T20Is, establishing himself as one of the formidable players in the shortest format.But it is somewhere between captaincy duties and explosive hitting that he'd need to find perfect cohesion. The Giants are yearning for their first ILT20 title since 2023. After that glorious run and an exit in the second qualifier in 2024, they've finished fifth in the last two seasons and missed out on making the playoffs. In the opening season of the competition in the UAE, the Giants topped the points table before winning a comfortable final against the Desert Vipers. The owners and coach Simon Helmot would expect much of the same from Klaasen & Co."The batting aspect shouldn't have anything to do with the captaincy. I think that's where the balance needs to come in. I need to be free enough to still play the aggressive brand of cricket I normally play, or the normal way I play. And then on the field is where the captaincy and my brand has to work a little bit different," Klaasen explained his philosophy as he prepared to play the ILT20 for the first time.The Gulf Giants will open their ILT20 campaign against the Sharjah Warriorz at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Sunday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aneurin Donald: Welsh T20 batter hopes for England chance in Australia
articles.summary: Welsh batter Aneurin Donald is part of England's T20 squad for the five-match series in Australia, and hoping to play his part at the MCG.
articles.body:
From Gorseinon cricket club in Swansea to some of the most famous grounds in Australia.

That is the journey England's latest Welsh batter Aneurin Donald is preparing to complete when the T20 five-match series starts against Australia on Saturday.

Donald made his England debut in the home three-match series against Sri Lanka but this tour represents a step up.

It is 12,000 miles between the Swansea suburb and the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) where the first game is being played.

It is a journey that has taken many years since starting at his local cricket club.

He originally came down with his father Andrew to watch the local rugby club but became hooked on cricket.

"Gorseinon means so much to me," said Donald, speaking to the BBC at the Welfare Ground, where the two clubs are based.

"My family and friends are so involved down here and I spent so much time there growing up as a kid, playing rugby and cricket.

"I try and get back there as much as I can. It's the lifeblood of the community and the reason I got the chances I did.

"The basis that I gathered here, the time and energy I spent training in the winter got me on the rung to professional sport and now an international cap."

England's Donald ready to savour Welsh homecoming

The Gorseinon work ethic and Leigh Halfpenny effect

The one-lane indoor net, now called the Alan Jones indoor cricket centre after Gorseinon’s other England batter, helped shape Donald’s talent.

"That one little indoor net lane we had is probably the big reason as to why I've made it as far as I have," said Donald.

"It was a little tin shed with probably a five-yard run-up where my brother [Gafyn] used to bowl into the middle of my bat.

"It was a massive part of my career now."

Those nets included training when others were relaxing.

"If I had to put one thing down in my junior years and what separated me was probably coming down and training and being able to use that little indoor shed," he adds.

"My dad installed a belief in me if I was training on a day nobody else is, you have added that little extra, whatever time of year.

"We used to go down every week and I can remember training on Christmas Eve.

"It was freezing cold and I remember being wrapped up in scarves and there was ice on our breath."

While the Donalds were freezing inside, outside honing his kicking skills was a Wales rugby icon who also started his sporting journey at Gorseinon.

"We used to see Leigh Halfpenny kicking for hours on end and it's probably a reminder that work ethic is what makes great players like him great," said Donald.

"I can’t compare my career with his but I took inspiration from seeing him out there."

Donald’s dedication has had to be matched by his resolve.

His road to international cricket proved longer than most, having to recover from two serious knee injuries.

After starting his career with Glamorgan, he moved on to Hampshire and Derbyshire, where he has established himself as the explosive specialist short form batter he now is.

His England recognition came later than most at the age of 29 with his three T20 appearances against Sri Lanka in September.

There was a game on Welsh soil in Cardiff after his debut in Southampton, where he was awarded his cap by England consultant Kevin Pietersen in front of his parents and girlfriend Heather.

"That was the one moment I will never forget," said Donald.

"It was special to be there with my parents who've put all those miles, time, money and energy into me, and my girlfriend who supports me when I am travelling around the world and holds the fort down back home.

"That's the one image that's been in my mind that I'll never forget.

"It lasted for 30 seconds, an amazing speech from KP and suddenly it's, run upstairs, stick your pads on, get out there and try and do your job."

Mixed feelings about first England series

Donald had a strike rate of 191 in the series, emphasising his role in attacking from the first ball to set the tone for the innings.

He would have liked to have scored more than 46 runs in his three innings - with a top score of 21- although he says he had the full support of captain Harry Brook and coach Brendon McCullum.

"I could have gone worse and got out for three ducks, so it was better than that.

"I showed a little bit of a glimpse of what I can do and the way I want to play.

"Baz [McCullum] and Brookie are supportive of that and that's exactly why I was picked.

"My job is to come out swinging and get the boys ahead of the game.

"I'd like to be sat here with a bigger score under my belt, but I think I have shown I can throw some punches at that level."

Donald says he was not affected by nerves.

"Walking out to bat with Jos Buttler, someone I've idolised, as friends and batting partners, is mad and probably still hasn't sunk in yet," he added.

"Oddly I felt pretty calm, it may have been a little bit because I was older and gone through the ups and downs in my career.

"So I didn't feel anywhere near as nervous as I thought. If this was going to be my only crack, I'm going to enjoy.

"It came and went so quickly with three games in five days.

"Hopefully I get a few more opportunities down the line. It is still mad how quickly things have happened these last few months."

Will two Welsh-born batters open for England in Australia?

Those further opportunities could come in Australia, after he was named in the squad for the five-match series that starts on Saturday.

"If you ask any young cricketer in England and Wales they're probably going to mention touring Australia as pretty high up on the list," said Donald.

"To play at some of those iconic venues, with that first game at the MCG would be a special moment.

"Whether I get a crack or not, it's going to be a different challenge again, an overseas tour in a hostile environment against a strong team.”

Donald’s chance came when fellow Welshman Phil Salt was injured. With Salt back and Buttler missing because of a hamstring problem, there could be two Welsh batters at the top of the order, with the in-form Tom Banton also in the equation.

"To walk out with Salty, north and south Wales, where we've got a lot of bases covered there, would be a proud moment, not just for us, but for Welsh cricket also,” said Donald.

"To show we can produce some players on the world stage and guys who can kick it at any level.

"Ever since making my debut, whether that's domestically or internationally, the support I've had from Welsh cricket and the wider Welsh community has always been incredible.”

Donald will stay in Australia after the series because he has picked up a contract with Perth Scorchers in the Big Bash league. He will then join Joburg Super Kings in the Betway SA20 in South Africa, which starts in late January.

"The franchise world has opened all sorts of doors,” said Donald.

"To get your foot in the door in one of the top three leagues in the world was a massive moment.

"It was a big feather in my cap to be able to go to the Perth Scorchers.”

This is the cricket life Donald is following, with stints in leagues in Canada, the Netherlands and UAE. The Indian Premier League (IPL) remains the ultimate T20 goal.

“The skill sets in the shorter format are getting better from probably even when I first started 10-15 years ago," he adds.

"The amount of opportunities out there for T20 cricket, and the lifestyle it gives you where you can travel the world and play with the best, is a special place to be."

He says it "would be silly" currently not to double down on what he is good at, even if he still wants to play the longer form of the game.

"I am desperate to keep playing red ball, certainly in the county game," he added.

"There's very few guys realistically who can cruise around from franchise to franchise and make a living.

"There's always a bit of a balance, but white ball is the forefront for me at the moment.”

articles.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal-KL Rahul script history: Produce India's best opening stand in New Zealand in 36 years, end 17-Test drought
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul gave India a much-needed solid start in reply to New Zealand's imposing first-innings total, putting together a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul gave India a much-needed solid start in reply to New Zealand's imposing first-innings total, putting together a 130-run opening partnership on the second day of the first Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Friday. It was India's second-highest opening-wicket stand in Tests in New Zealand and their best in the country in 36 years.The left-right combination looked increasingly comfortable as the innings progressed, negotiating the new ball and making the most of a batting-friendly surface. Their 130-run stand was bettered only by Manoj Prabhakar and WV Raman's unbeaten 149-run partnership against New Zealand in Auckland in February 1990.It also ended a significant drought for India. This was their first century partnership for the opening wicket in 17 Tests, spanning 30 innings. The last such stand had come in November 2024, when Jaiswal and Rahul themselves put together 201 runs in the Perth Test against Australia.Jaiswal was particularly fluent, striking 16 boundaries in his 89-ball 85. He looked set for a well-deserved century before Matt Henry finally broke the partnership in the 28th over.The New Zealand pacer was convinced there had been an edge when Jaiswal attempted to defend a short-of-a-length delivery that moved away. Tom Blundell, standing up to the stumps, completed the catch, although he initially did not appear convinced. Henry persisted with his appeal, and the review confirmed a faint edge.The dismissal ended a commanding opening stand and gave the hosts a breakthrough after India had steadily built momentum.Nicholls' marathon knock takes New Zealand to 368Earlier, Henry Nicholls remained stranded on 175 as New Zealand were bowled out for 368 in their first innings. The left-hander batted for close to 10 hours, facing 335 deliveries and striking 21 boundaries in one of his finest Test innings.His 216-run sixth-wicket partnership with Glenn Phillips, who scored 118 off 216 balls, rescued New Zealand from a precarious 70/5 and put the hosts firmly in control.For India, Jasprit Bumrah led the bowling effort with 4/92 from 29 overs, while Akash Deep claimed 3/53 in 23 overs. Anshul Kamboj picked up two wickets for 69 runs, while Prasidh Krishna returned 1/100 from 26 overs.Phillips completed his second Test century against the second new ball, but Akash Deep eventually ended his resistance with a delivery that shaped in before nipping away to clip the top of off stump.India's bowling effort, particularly with the second new ball, left questions over the effectiveness of Prasidh and Kamboj, while the decision not to open the second day's attack with Akash Deep also came under scrutiny.However, Jaiswal and Rahul's remarkable partnership ensured India finished the day with a significant response to New Zealand's first-innings effort.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australian government urges CA to ensure transparency in inquiry as sandpapergate row refuses to fade
articles.summary: Cricket Australia has been urged to ensure that its proposed forum into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal is conducted independently and with as much
articles.body: Cricket Australia has been urged to ensure that its proposed forum into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal is conducted independently and with as much transparency as possible, with a government spokesperson making the appeal on Friday amid criticism from former players over the governing body's handling of the controversy.CA announced on Wednesday that it would set up an independent forum where players could share their accounts of the incident. However, the governing body said the findings would not necessarily be made public and no sanctions would follow.The decision has drawn criticism from former players and commentators, including former Australia captain Michael Clarke, who said the public had been misled about how many people were involved in the ball-tampering during the Test series in South Africa.A spokesperson for Australian sports minister Anika Wells said integrity was important to "every kid with a bat or a ball"."This is Cricket Australia's process to run and it is a matter for them to work through. Australians will expect this to be run independently and as openly as possible," the spokesperson said in a statement."We have a summer of cricket to look forward to and I'm sure all of Australia will get behind our team."No prior knowledgeThe eight-year-old Sandpapergate controversy resurfaced this month after former Australia batter Usman Khawaja alleged that more players and support staff knew about the ball-tampering than the three who were found responsible and punished following an investigation by CA's integrity unit during the South Africa tour.CA had banned then-captain Steve Smith and David Warner for 12 months, while Cameron Bancroft received a nine-month ban.Current Test captain Pat Cummins and fellow fast bowler Mitchell Starc have rejected Khawaja's claims, saying they had no prior knowledge of the ball-tampering.However, three other players who were part of the 2018 tour have backed Khawaja's account. Warner and Bancroft were among them, with Bancroft saying "the whole team" knew about it, including members of the coaching staff and a media manager.Clarke, who captained Australia from 2011 to 2015, said CA's proposed forum had become unnecessary after Bancroft shared a 4,000-word statement with the media on Wednesday."The public don’t want any more bullshit,” he said on his podcast "Beyond23".“The public want the complete truth to allow us to move on."The controversy has also increased pressure on Cummins, who has several corporate sponsors.Last week, Cummins rejected Khawaja's allegations as "complete and utter nonsense" during an hour-long press conference. He also criticised his former teammate for being "casual" with other people's lives and reputations.Cummins did not speak to reporters gathered outside his Sydney home on Thursday or at training. However, his manager said the Australia captain's position remained unchanged and he had no reason to respond to Bancroft's statement.A poll of 13,000 readers conducted by Melbourne's Herald Sun newspaper found that 82% believed the accounts given by Khawaja, Warner and Bancroft, while 18% backed Cummins and Australia's bowlers, who have denied having prior knowledge of the ball-tampering.In a separate poll by the Sydney Morning Herald, a majority of 6,000 readers said they did not expect Cummins to remain captain for the first Test of the home summer against New Zealand, which begins on December 9.Former Australia fast bowler Mitchell Johnson also said the public pressure on Cummins to step down as captain would become too great."I just can’t see how his captaincy and personal brand survives this," Johnson wrote in a column for The West Australian newspaper.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: One boundary at a time, Yashasvi Jaiswal deflates New Zealand
articles.summary: WELLINGTON: Straight as an arrow, Yashasvi Jaiswal smoked one past Jacob Duffy to bring up his half-century off 66 balls.
articles.body: WELLINGTON: Straight as an arrow, Yashasvi Jaiswal smoked one past Jacob Duffy to bring up his half-century off 66 balls. Another boundary, a rare scratchy one, followed the next ball as the southpaw moved to 54 with his tenth four of the innings. India had already surpassed their previous best opening stand of 73 in this part of the world, dating back to 2009, and Jaiswal was throwing punches with sublime strokeplay.There were no half-measures. He drove beautifully, wasn't afraid to deploy the ramp and kept finding gaps with ease against New Zealand's seamers. The left-handed batter operated with a lot of assurance after giving the new ball the required respect and never looked back. There was a lot of arrogance in the way he went about his business, bordering on audacity against a potent bowling attack featuring Jacob Duffy, Kyle Jamieson and Nathan Smith.The calmness of KL Rahul at the other end was the perfect antidote as the two stitched together a fluent partnership to give India a solid start to their innings. Rahul was lucky to survive an LBW shout early in the innings, but he hardly drew attention as Jaiswal stepped on the gas. The 24-year-old hit 16 boundaries during his knock, and his intent after reaching his half-century blew the Kiwis away.The next 35 runs came off just 32 deliveries, with 28 of those runs scored in boundaries. Jacob Duffy struggled, and Jaiswal never allowed any fast bowler in the opposition camp to find rhythm. His footwork remained precise, and his shot selection was impeccable. Except for that wild hoick moments after his fifty, Jaiswal largely played on merit and operated with a watertight defence off the back foot.The youngster featured in three India A-New Zealand A fixtures before the Test series and came well prepared for the two-match series. His starts in those fixtures were subdued, but he roared back with scores of 155* and 102 and carried the confidence from those games into the Wellington opener. Jaiswal's runs and intent not only wiped off the valuable deficit but also deflated the opposition by not allowing them an opportunity to stitch together a plan.With nothing happening off the surface or in the air, and the ball losing its sheen off Jaiswal's willow, the hosts threw a desperate dice by bringing the wicketkeeper up to the opener. Not that Jaiswal was walking into his shots, but it was just an attempt to make things happen when he wasn't allowing anything to happen.The move gave the hosts their first and only success of the day as Jaiswal nicked one to Tom Blundell off Matt Henry to end his entertaining 89-ball essay. Head down, he dragged himself back to the dressing room to a roaring applause, well aware that a big score was there for the taking. His 85 helped India put 130 on the board in just 27.5 overs and could well have delivered a decisive blow to the opposition.Brief ScoresNew Zealand 1st innings: 368 all out in 121 overs (Henry Nicholls 175, Glenn Phillips 118; Jasprit Bumrah 4/92, Akash Deep 3/53)India 1st innings: 159 for 1 after 39 overs (Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, KL Rahul 52 batting; Matt Henry 1/43)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Henry Nicholls scripts history vs India, breaks 36-year-old record with unbeaten 175 in first Test
articles.summary: Henry Nicholls has set a New Zealand record for the highest score by a No. 3 batter in a Test innings against India.
articles.body: Henry Nicholls has set a New Zealand record for the highest score by a No. 3 batter in a Test innings against India. The 34-year-old left-hander went past Andrew Jones' previous record on the second day of the ongoing first Test between India and New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Friday.Jones had scored an unbeaten 170 off 446 balls while batting at No. 3 in the second innings of the February 1990 Test at Eden Park in Auckland. His innings included 15 fours and two sixes. Nicholls, meanwhile, scored 175 off 335 balls, hitting 21 fours, before the end of 120 overs in New Zealand's first innings.Nicholls, who brought up his 12th Test century on Thursday, is only the second New Zealand No. 3 batter to score 150 or more in a Test innings against India.He shared a 216-run stand for the sixth wicket with Glenn Phillips, who scored 118 off 216 balls. The partnership helped New Zealand recover from 70/5 and take their first-innings total past 300.If Nicholls scores another 25 runs to reach 200, he will become only the fifth New Zealand batter to score a double century in a Test innings against India.Bert Sutcliffe, Graham Dowling, Brendon McCullum and Jesse Ryder are the only New Zealand batters to have scored 200 or more runs in a Test innings against India. McCullum has achieved the feat three times, scoring two double centuries and a triple century.Jaiswal, Rahul put India in command after Nicholls' 175 powers NZ to 368Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul helped India reach 159/1 at stumps on Day 2 after New Zealand were bowled out for 368 in their first innings of the opening Test in Wellington on Friday.Jaiswal scored 85 off 89 balls, hitting 16 fours, while sharing a 130-run opening stand with Rahul, who was unbeaten on 52 at the close of play.Devdutt Padikkal was batting on 16 alongside Rahul, with India trailing New Zealand by 209 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Match is evenly poised': Glenn Phillips expects spin to come into play as India build momentum vs New Zealand
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Glenn Phillips believes the opening Test between India and New Zealand at the Basin Reserve is evenly poised, but expects spin to become a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Glenn Phillips believes the opening Test between India and New Zealand at the Basin Reserve is evenly poised, but expects spin to become a factor as the contest progresses, with the pitch beginning to slow down and offer less bounce.India finished Day 2 at 159/1 in their first innings, trailing New Zealand by 209 runs after Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul put together an impressive 130-run opening partnership. New Zealand had earlier been bowled out for 368, with Phillips and Henry Nicholls rescuing the innings through a 216-run sixth-wicket stand after the hosts had slumped to 70/5."The match is evenly poised, India made great use of the new ball. We take 368 after put into bat first. Great partnership by two India openers. Pitch getting slower and lower, it will be about playing the long game," Phillips said at the post-play press conference.Jaiswal struck 85 off 89 deliveries, hitting 16 fours, while Rahul remained unbeaten on 52. Devdutt Padikkal was batting on 16 at stumps, with India looking to build on their strong start.Phillips backs spin to have a role as pitch slows downAlthough the Basin Reserve is traditionally regarded as a venue favouring fast bowlers, Phillips believes the conditions could bring the spinners into the contest."Need for spinner from one end hasn’t come yet. Lets hope there is some spin and bounce, and I can contribute. Wellington gets a bad rap that it's a seam bowling friendly pitch. Both me and Lyon have taken five wickets each in second innings. We have Rachin as well. Tommy can use us both if needed. Me, Washi and Rachin will have a role when the game progresses," he said.Phillips, who scored 118 off 216 balls, was referring to the potential roles of New Zealand's spin options, including Rachin Ravindra, as well as India's Washington Sundar, as the surface wears.The all-rounder also reflected on the challenges of fielding at the Basin Reserve, particularly when stationed close to the square."This place sucks to catch. If you are square of the wicket, two feet in front of you to see. articles.title: Rawalpindi Test: Pakistan end two-year drought as Sri Lanka suffer historic low with four straight away series defeats
articles.summary: A new-look Pakistan side ended a two-year wait for a Test series triumph, overpowering Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the second Test in Rawalpindi on
articles.body: A new-look Pakistan side ended a two-year wait for a Test series triumph, overpowering Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the second Test in Rawalpindi on Friday to clinch the two-match series 1-0. The defeat extended Sri Lanka's miserable overseas run, leaving them with four successive away Test series losses and a calendar year without a single Test victory for the first time since 1997.Chasing a modest target after restricting Sri Lanka to 316 in their second innings, Pakistan raced to 90/2 in just 13 overs during the first session on Day 4. Aamer Jamal provided the finishing flourish with an unbeaten 34 off 22 balls, smashing five fours and a six, while Azan Awais remained not out on 32.The victory was Pakistan's first Test series win since beating England at home in October 2024. It was also only their third win in 11 matches in the current World Test Championship cycle.Pakistan captain Babar Azam was particularly pleased with the way his relatively inexperienced side responded to the challenge."Very satisfying, the way the team performed. We had a young team, many players grabbed their opportunities. The environment in the dressing room is very positive, we just need to stay stable and focus on the game. All the players gave 100% to their roles and that was nice to see," Babar said.Sri Lanka's overseas struggles deepenThe series defeat added another unwanted chapter to Sri Lanka's recent Test record. Their last overseas series victory came against Bangladesh in March 2024, and they have now lost four consecutive away series.The Islanders will also finish 2026 without a Test victory for the first time since 1997. Pakistan, meanwhile, have won three of their last four Test series against Sri Lanka, whose previous series triumph over Pakistan came in September 2017.Sri Lanka's troubles in Rawalpindi began in the first innings when Pakistan's seamers bowled them out for just 98 inside the first two sessions on the opening day. The visitors conceded a massive 227-run first-innings lead, leaving themselves with a mountain to climb.They showed greater resistance in the second innings, with Milan Rathnayake remaining unbeaten on 66 to help extend the contest. However, Mohammad Abbas, who claimed 3/55 in the innings, ended the resistance by trapping Asitha Fernando lbw in his first over on Friday.Abbas, who was named both Player of the Match and Player of the Series, said his performance had been overdue."The performance was due, I spoke before the series and the challenges before it, still have to take a 5-wicket haul, hopefully I will do it. I assess the conditions, make sure that my economy is low and it helps the other bowlers as well. I only advised them to hit the areas well, Saqib became unfit unfortunately, that made my responsibility more," he said.Babar praises youngsters as Mendis looks aheadPakistan's victory was particularly encouraging given the number of fresh faces in the squad, with four players making their debuts during the series. Babar singled out wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi for making the most of his opportunities and also credited fast bowler Razaullah's pace and first-innings contribution."If you have a bowler who can bowl at 145 kmph, it gives you confidence. His spell in the first innings was vital and that was one of the main reasons for our series win today," Babar said.Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis acknowledged that his side's poor first-innings batting had proved costly."Honestly, we didn't bat well in the first innings, including me. I got out at a crucial time. We bowled well and batted well in the 2nd innings. Bowling wise, I thought we hit the areas well," Mendis said.He also thanked Pakistan for hosting the team during a tour that included a 2-1 T20I series defeat and a loss in the ODI tri-series final."We've stayed here for more than one month, we enjoyed Pakistan and have had positives in both Tests. The fast bowlers bowled well and I'm happy with the improvement. Looking forward to the tour of New Zealand. Hopefully, I will be back here in the PSL or some other tournament. I thank Pakistan for hosting us, we enjoyed our stay here," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Kaisa chal raha?’: Akash Deep reveals how Gautam Gambhir motivated him through lengthy injury layoff
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Akash Deep's return to Test cricket after a lengthy injury layoff was made more reassuring by the support he received from head coach Gautam
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Akash Deep's return to Test cricket after a lengthy injury layoff was made more reassuring by the support he received from head coach Gautam Gambhir during rehabilitation. The India fast bowler said Gambhir regularly checked on his progress, and those conversations kept him motivated through a challenging period away from the game.Akash, who had been out of top-flight cricket since August 2025 due to a stress fracture in his back, made an impressive comeback in the first Test against New Zealand, claiming three wickets as India bowled out the visitors for 368 in their first innings.Speaking after the second day's play, the Bengal pacer recalled how Gambhir stayed in touch while he was undergoing rehabilitation at the BCCI Centre of Excellence.“GG (Gambhir) sir used to follow up during that period and he would take updates — ‘Kaisa chal raha?’ he would ask,” Akash said.“Very difficult to come back after a back injury for a fast bowler. Coach was in touch with me during rehab, and it kept motivating me. I worked on skills, and never felt I was away from cricket for this long,” he added.ALSO READ: 50/4 and a lot of heat: How Akash Deep sparked India's turnaround on Day 2'I wanted to get stronger' during rehabilitationThe extended break was not just about regaining fitness. Akash used the time to work on his bowling and improve areas of his game, with his outings for India A also helping him build confidence before returning to the senior side.“During that time, I worked on my bowling and on areas I could improve. I wanted to get stronger. It didn't feel like I was playing international cricket after nearly one and a half years,” he said.“I was happy with what I bowled for India A,” he added.Akash made his comeback count with three for 53 against New Zealand. The dismissal of Glenn Phillips was among the highlights of his spell, as he came wide of the crease and delivered a ball that moved away after pitching to dislodge the batter's off-stump bail.Explaining the delivery, Akash said he had deliberately put in extra effort to generate movement and unsettle the batter.“On that Glenn Phillips wicket delivery, I put in extra effort ki ball zyaada harkat kare. I went wide of the crease to keep batter into play… start playing with batter’s mind,” he said.“It wasn't one (magic) ball. I was trying to bowl in one area. That ball I put in more effort and could get what I wanted to,” he added.Akash Deep on adapting to the pitchThe pacer also spoke about the changing conditions at the Basin Reserve, where the pitch had slowed down on the first day before offering some assistance with the new ball on the second.“Yesterday wicket got slower after Lunch, and today there was help with the new ball,” he said.Akash stressed that containing the scoring and sticking to a plan remained important, particularly when bowling with the older ball.“The first option with an old ball is to contain runs and then stick to a plan. My experience here is that you need to bowl to plan and stop the runs. Very difficult to come back after a back injury for a fast bowler,” he said.He also welcomed India's positive batting approach, with openers KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal putting together a brisk partnership.“We scored quickly and that's a positive sign. Whatever be the opposition, if batters attack like this, bowlers go on the back foot,” Akash said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia's Sandpapergate: Usman Khawaja called 'traitor' by former South Africa bowler for ball-tampering claims
articles.summary: Ex-South Africa bowler Fanie de Villiers says Usman Khawaja "broke every single code of conduct" with allegations in autobiography; Khawaja's claims since backed up by David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Cameron Bancroft; Dr Simon Longstaff feels Pat Cummins' denial of knowledge is "sincere"
articles.body:
Khawaja said in his autobiography that every member of the Australia team was aware of the plot to manipulate the ball with sandpaper on the 2018 South Africa tour, a claim backed up by David Warner , Chadd Sayers and, most explosively, Cameron Bancroft .

Bancroft - who, along with Warner and then-captain Steve Smith, served a ban following the rumbling of the ball-tampering plot - wrote in a 4,000-word-plus article in the West Australian newspaper that Pat Cummins' vehement denials made him break his silence.

Current Australia Test skipper Cummins stated in a 68-minute press conference last week that Khawaja's claims were "utter nonsense", which Bancroft said left him feeling "angry, betrayed and alone".

De Villiers, who played 18 Tests and 83 ODIs for South Africa between 1992 and 1998 told Perth's 91.3 SportFM , that Khawaja had "broken every single code of conduct".

The 62-year-old said: "I want to go on the record and say I think Khawaja is probably the biggest traitor that I've ever seen ... over my last 40, 50 years of watching the game.

"He's sold out his fellow players. This is not about right or wrong. The wrong has already been handled. It's already been part of Australian cricket, and it's sad that it happened.

"But this guy has brought everything to the fore again.

"He's brought Australian cricket in disrepute all over again, breaking down of friendships, the code of conduct that one has within the team, he's done everything wrong one can think of."

'I believe Cummins was sincere in press conference'

Dr Simon Longstaff, part of the cultural review into Australian cricket that Cricket Australia sanctioned after Sandpapergate, says he did not think Cummins was lying in his fiery press conference but also believes Bancroft's account of the saga.

"I think both (Cummins and Bancroft) have been sincere in what they're saying," Longstaff told Australian broadcaster Nine .

"It's possible, that as a very young, inexperienced bowler at the time, (Cummins) was having conversations about the ball without understanding the conditions under which it was being altered. That has got to be allowed still as a possibility.

"I've been around long enough and have investigated various problems of this kind, where people have sworn black and blue that they were telling the truth, and you eventually find out that they both were being sincere.

"It's possible to utter what is objectively false but not do so with any kind of inclination to lie, so I think it's something still in the middle of that that needs to be explored.

"What is clear now is that the whispers that I was hearing at the time line up pretty much with what Bancroft has said, including the timing for the first use of sandpaper.

"What's distressing is that when people were given the opportunity to tell the truth, including by me, they chose not to do so. And that's a stain that carries across to the team to this day."

Former England captain Michael Atherton said on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcas t that he does not expect Cummins to resign from his role as Test skipper.

Atherton said of the 33-year-old: "He's obviously got a lot of credit in the bank in terms of performance as captain, having transformed the culture and kept Australia at the top of the tree, if you like.

"So I don't think there's an immediate threat there."

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Sri Lankan great Mahela Jayawardene has joined Delhi Capitals as Director of Cricket for their Women's Premier League (WPL) team ahead of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sri Lankan great Mahela Jayawardene has joined Delhi Capitals as Director of Cricket for their Women's Premier League (WPL) team ahead of the 2027 season, bringing his considerable international and franchise cricket experience to the franchise's leadership setup.The JSW and GMR co-owned franchise announced the appointment on Friday, with Jayawardene set to oversee all cricketing matters, including team strategy, talent identification, and the development of players and coaching staff.The former Sri Lanka captain is among the most accomplished batters of his generation and has also established himself as a successful coach in franchise cricket. A three-time IPL-winning coach, Jayawardene's appointment is aimed at strengthening Delhi Capitals' cricketing structure as they look to build a consistent title-winning side in the WPL.Jayawardene brings leadership and coaching experienceJayawardene represented Sri Lanka in 149 Tests and 448 ODIs, scoring 11,814 and 12,650 runs respectively. He captained his country and was part of the Sri Lankan side that won the 2014 ICC World T20.After retiring from international cricket, he moved into coaching and developed a reputation for building competitive teams in franchise cricket. Delhi Capitals will now look to draw on that experience as they seek to strengthen their women's setup and challenge for the WPL title.“Delhi Capitals has a strong identity and an exciting vision for the future of women’s cricket. I am delighted to take on the role of Director of Cricket for the WPL team. The competition has enormous potential to shape the future of the women’s game, and I look forward to working with an established group of talented players and an experienced support team,” Jayawardene said.“My focus will be on building on the team’s existing strengths, bringing greater consistency to performances and ensuring we continue to evolve and compete for the title. I am excited about what we can achieve together,” he added.Delhi Capitals target sustained success in WPLThe franchise's leadership believes Jayawardene's appointment will add strategic depth and strengthen its long-term plans for the women's team.Kiran Kumar Grandhi, co-owner of Delhi Capitals and chairman of GMR Sports, said the franchise wanted to build on the foundations established in the WPL and create a team capable of consistently challenging for the title.“Mahela's appointment brings an added dimension of experience and strategic leadership to the women's setup. His understanding of the modern game and experience in building competitive teams will be valuable in taking Delhi Capitals Women to the next level,” Grandhi said.Parth Jindal, chairman and co-owner of Delhi Capitals and founder of JSW Sports, also welcomed the appointment, describing Jayawardene as “one of the finest cricketing minds in the game”.Delhi Capitals CEO Sunil Gupta called it a significant step towards building a world-class women's cricket team and establishing a sustained culture of excellence.Jayawardene's arrival marks a fresh move in Delhi Capitals' preparations for the 2027 WPL season, with the franchise hoping his experience and vision can help them take the next step in their pursuit of the title.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Scotland lose Super Six opening thriller to Netherlands
articles.summary: Scotland fall to a final-over, seven-wicket defeat by the Netherlands in their opening match in the Super Six stage of the Women's Emerging Nations Trophy.
articles.body:
Scotland 154-7 (20 overs): K Bryce 34, Fraser 25; De Lange 2-19

Netherlands 155-3 (19.4 overs): Kalis 52, Molkenboer 43; K Bryce 1-32

Scotland fell to a final-over, seven-wicket defeat by the Netherlands in their opening match in the Super Six stage of the Women's Emerging Nations Trophy.

The Scots, who qualified second in their group behind Sri Lanka in Dubai, reached 154-7 in their innings.

But the Dutch, who were second behind Pakistan in their section, surpassed that for the loss of just three wickets, albeit with only two balls to spare.

Scotland captain Kathryn Bryce said: "I feel like the pitch changed significantly in the second innings, but I still felt we had a total on the board that we should have been able to defend.

"We weren't able to have a good period of pressure on them - probably gave them too many boundary balls early on and they batted nicely.

"It's not great margins. It's just being a little bit sharper and more switched on in different areas."

Scotland sink Ireland as both reach Super Six phase

Dutch captain Sterre Kalis led from the front with an unbeaten, 27-ball 52 as her side go second in the table behind Sri Lanka.

Scotland had reached 60 before the loss of the first wicket, Katherine Fraser having hit 25.

However, the run rate declined after captain Bryce was bowled for 34 with her side on 123-4, although Pippa Sproul finished unbeaten on 23.

The Dutch put on 87 for the first wicket before Sanya Khurana was run out for 41.

Fellow opener Phebe Molkenboer helped add seven more runs to the total before she was out for 43.

But Kalis took up the challenge with six fours and two sixes in her half-century before the victory was sealed with a two leg-byes from the fourth ball of the final over.

Scotland's second defeat of the tournament leaves them sitting third in the table before Pakistan and Ireland play their game in hand later in the day.

The Scots next face Pakistan on Sunday as the Dutch take on Sri Lanka.

articles.title: 'They will have to face this': Irfan Pathan predicts Sandpapergate storm for Australia during 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy
articles.summary: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan believes Australia's fresh ball-tampering scandal revelations could come back to haunt Pat Cummins and his team when
articles.body: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan believes Australia's fresh ball-tampering scandal revelations could come back to haunt Pat Cummins and his team when they tour India for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy next year. With the controversy back in the spotlight following explosive claims by Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft, Pathan feels the Australian players will face considerable scrutiny from Indian fans and the media.The 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as 'Sandpapergate', has once again sparked debate after Khawaja and Bancroft suggested that knowledge of the controversial sandpaper tactic extended beyond the players who were directly punished. Their revelations have also raised fresh questions about collective responsibility within the Australian dressing room during the Test series against South Africa.While Cummins dismissed Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense", Bancroft's detailed account in The West Australian offered further insight into the incident. The opener recalled discussions about reverse swing with Australia's bowlers, including Cummins, and claimed that his actions were encouraged, with several members of the team aware of the plan.Speaking on JioStar, Pathan said the fresh revelations would ensure that Australia remain under the scanner when they arrive in India for the five-match Border-Gavaskar Trophy series in January 2027.'There will be a lot of talk': Irfan Pathan warns Australia ahead of India tourPathan believes the controversy will follow the Australian team throughout their India tour, with Cummins and his teammates needing to be mentally prepared to deal with questions surrounding the scandal."I am pretty sure that when Australia comes down to India to play the BGT series, there will be a lot of talk around it. Wherever the Australians will go, they will have to face this. And they will have to be mentally strong to handle this, because it is all out there in the public domain," Pathan said.Pathan questions David Warner's timing in addressing SandpapergatePathan also questioned former Australia opener David Warner's decision to raise concerns about the investigation years after the incident. Warner, along with Steve Smith and Bancroft, was sanctioned following the scandal, with Warner receiving a leadership ban and a lifetime ban from holding a leadership position in Australian cricket.Pathan felt Warner should have spoken up at the time rather than questioning the investigation years later. He also pointed out that Cricket Australia's investigation had identified Warner, who was vice-captain at the time, as the player who initiated the plan to tamper with the ball."I personally believe that Warner, because he has been through a ban, should have spoken then and there. Now, nothing can happen. The investigation happened over four days. Cricket Australia did what they thought was best at that particular time," he said."What I'm assuming from the investigation is that, because David Warner was the vice-captain, he was the one who initiated doing something with the ball. This is what the investigation by Cricket Australia established, and that's why it came out and he was punished."Now, to talk about it and say that it was a shady investigation, I think it is too late. He should have spoken then and there, and things would have been very different," Pathan added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pat Cummins retains support of Cricket Australia as Test captain despite sandpaper allegations
articles.summary: Pat Cummins will retain backing from Cricket Australia to remain as Test captain despite ongoing and explosive allegations about the sandpaper controversy.
articles.body:
Pat Cummins will retain backing from Cricket Australia (CA) to remain as Test captain despite ongoing and explosive allegations about the sandpaper controversy.

A detailed testimony from Cameron Bancroft supported previous claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team – including Cummins – knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test match against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.

Cummins has always denied involvement in or knowledge of the cheating plot, and reiterated his stance in a 68-minute address to the media last week.

CA has regularly spoken of its support for Cummins, and the fast bowler will be allowed to continue in the captaincy role he has held since 2021. A statement could be issued over the weekend.

Cummins, 33, is due to lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand on 9 December. A squad for the series opener against the Black Caps has not yet been named.

With the support of CA, a decision on Cummins' future as captain would now appear to rest with the player, who has shown no indication he will resign.

The row over the sandpaper saga, one of the biggest controversies in Test history, has engulfed Australian sport since Khawaja's claims first emerged two weeks ago.

In 2018, Bancroft, then-captain Steve Smith and his vice-captain David Warner were punished for Bancroft's act of rubbing sandpaper on the ball in the third Test against South Africa at Newlands.

Khawaja, who retired from international cricket earlier this year, wrote in his autobiography that the entire Australian team knew and should have taken responsibility.

The former batter's account was supported by his childhood friend Warner, along with Chadd Sayers and Jon Holland, both back-up bowlers on the tour.

In response, Cummins called a news conference where he promised to answer all questions about his part in the controversy, in the hope of "never having to speak about it again".

He called Khawaja's assertions "100% wrong" and "nonsense".

However, Cummins' address to the media motivated Bancroft to publish his own account of more than 4,000 words in the West Australian newspaper.

"The final straw for me to write this account was Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins' press conference," said Bancroft.

"It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone."

Bancroft alleged he had conversations with all of the bowlers about how much the ball was swinging, and that the entire group of players and coaches celebrated when the ball-tampering yielded success.

Batter Bancroft also implicated Darren Lehmann, who was then the Australia head coach, and David Saker, the bowling coach.

Lehmann, now the coach of county side Northamptonshire, is due to commentate for the BBC and Australian radio station ABC on the first T20 between Australia and England in Melbourne on Saturday.

Saker was part of the England coaching staff for the one-day tri-series in Pakistan in October.

The 60-year-old has been employed by England on an ad hoc consultancy basis, an arrangement that has now ended.

England have firmed up new coaching teams under Test head coach Stephen Fleming and his white-ball counterpart Brendon McCullum.

articles.title: England in Australia: T20 cricket the new focus as batters bowl, Adil Rashid eyes recall and 'Sandpapergate' rumbles on
articles.summary: England begin five-match T20 series against beleaguered Australia in Melbourne on Saturday (8.15am UK); Harry Brook's side looking to build-on ODI series win as Adil Rashid eyes recall after being omitted for 50-over matches; Mitchell Marsh does not appear at pre-series press conference
articles.body:
That was Michael Atherton's take on Australia before the 'Sandpapergate' scandal spectacularly hit the headlines once again following Usman Khawaja's claims in his autobiography.

Three weeks ago, the biggest problems for the Baggy Greens were Test batting woes, including a bang-out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne, and some odd selection decisions.

That "implosion" Athers predicted on the field has come off it, with David Warner and Cameron Bancroft supporting Khawaja's account that all members of the team were aware of the sandpaper scheme in 2018, and Pat Cummins strenuously denying it.

Australian cricket is at civil war and there is no obvious end in sight.

Questions abound (will Cummins survive as captain? Will Steve Smith, Nathan Lyon and Josh Hazlewood have their say? Does Cricket Australia have any choice but to launch a fresh investigation and not just an open forum?) but answers are in short supply.

England looking to pile more misery on Australia

Runs were also in short supply for Australia in the final two ODIs against England as a side helmed by Mitchell Marsh in the absence of the rested (but surely mentally tired) Cummins were twice bundled out in the low 200s chasing targets of 320-plus.

That meant Harry Brook's tourists were able to bounce back from being pummelled in Perth in the opening fixture - a result which brought back horrible memories of their Ashes thrashing at the venue a year ago - to claim a come-from-behind 2-1 series win.

They will now look to pile the misery on their beleaguered hosts with victory in a five-match T20 international series, starting in Melbourne on Saturday (first ball at 8.15am UK time).

At times in the ODIs, it felt like England were toying with an Australia team whose minds were perhaps understandably elsewhere. Jofra Archer sent out to bat at No 6 in Hobart, for example, and also Brook and Tom Banton being asked to deliver their part-time off-spin.

If Archer's elevation was a one-off - it certainly won't be seen in the T20s with the England quick rested as he prepares for the three-Test assignment in South Africa from December 17 - then the use of Brook and Banton with the ball may be a more regular occurrence, especially in 50-over cricket as Brendon McCullum's side laser in on the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

Head coach McCullum said: "These guys are talented, there is something there.

"We are looking at a World Cup in 12 months' time, and no one knows what the conditions are going to be like. You could end up on a pitch that is exploding and need some options.

"We will keep encouraging them to do that. That World Cup is potentially 13 games in three different countries, fresh pitches, there's not much data on how those pitches will play."

Marsh not expected to attend press conferences during series

Brook and Banton bowled 2.5 overs between them in the ODI series, which is 2.5 overs more than Adil Rashid. The frontline spinner had ample time to pour over the sandpaper storm after being left out for all three games, with Liam Dawson once again favoured.

Rashid will hope to be recalled for the T20s, starting at the weekend on a ground where he helped England beat Pakistan in the 2022 T20 World Cup final. The 38-year-old has played in all 19 of his side's T20Is in 2026, appearing alongside Dawson in 18 of them.

Brook, like Rashid, has fond memories of the MCG. He, too, was part of the T20 World Cup-winning squad four years ago, while he top-scored in a blink-and-you'll-miss-it, two-day Ashes Test there last winter as England claimed their only win of a sobering tour.

Brook was all smiles during his pre-series media duties in Melbourne on Friday, saying he wanted to guide his side to a 4-0 lead over Australia before he departs for the South Africa tour ahead of the series finale in Canberra on December 2.

He also spoke of his excitement that the uncapped James Coles, Henry Crocombe, Eddie Jack and Thomas Rew were able to experience being in an England squad in Australia, albeit without confirming if or when they would make their T20I debuts.

We do not know how Australia skipper Marsh is feeling, though, with the 34-year-old not expected to engage in any media activity with the written press throughout the T20 leg following Bancroft's explosive claims in that detail-filled account in the West Australian.

Marsh was part of the XI for the now infamous Cape Town Test eight years ago.

Cummins, Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc will not feature in the series at all as chat regarding what they did or did not know about the sandpaper use runs rampant.

Cummins and Hazlewood are rested, like they were for the ODIs, while Starc, who also sat out the 50-over encounters, has retired from international 20-over cricket.

Make no mistake, though. The heat is very much on them.

On the field, the heat will be on Marsh and an inexperienced bowling attack - weakened further by injuries to Mahli Beardman (quad) and Xavier Bartlett (knee) - to contain an England side that, despite missing the injured Jacob Bethell and Jos Buttler, is formidable.

Australia will also be out to avoid the top-order collapses of the final two ODIs, a goal that could be made easier by Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker joining Archer in being rested ahead of the red-ball trip to South Africa, which you can watch live on Sky Sports .

What the home side want most, however, is a series win over England and for all this sandpaper chat to stop. The first of those objectives looks tough. The second impossible.

Second T20I: Tuesday November 24 (Carrara)

Third T20I: Friday November 27 (Brisbane)

Fourth T20I: Sunday November 29 (Sydney)

Fifth T20I: Wednesday December 2 (Canberra)

articles.title: 'We've got all bases covered': Ricky Ponting explains PBKS' strategy behind retaining 19 players and trading for Hardik Pandya
articles.summary: Punjab Kings head coach Ricky Ponting believes the addition of Hardik Pandya has given the franchise a well-rounded squad, with the all-rounder bringing
articles.body: Punjab Kings head coach Ricky Ponting believes the addition of Hardik Pandya has given the franchise a well-rounded squad, with the all-rounder bringing greater balance and flexibility ahead of IPL 2027. Punjab made a major move in the trade window by securing Pandya from Mumbai Indians in exchange for India pacer Arshdeep Singh, with the deal completed at Rs 18 crore for each player.The trade marks a significant change for both franchises, with Pandya ending his second stint at Mumbai Indians to join Punjab, while Arshdeep moves to the five-time IPL champions after eight seasons with PBKS.With the retention deadline now behind them, Punjab have retained 19 players and released six, choosing to keep the core of their squad together as they prepare for the next three-year cycle. Ponting believes Pandya's presence, alongside several other versatile players, will give the team multiple options with both bat and ball.Speaking to JioStar, the former Australia captain explained the franchise's retention strategy and how the new addition has strengthened their squad.'We've got a very well-rounded squad': Ponting on Hardik Pandya's arrivalPonting said Punjab were keen to retain the majority of their existing players while making selective changes to improve the squad. He highlighted the number of all-rounders available to the franchise, believing their presence would help cover different combinations and playing conditions."I've been really conscious of trying to keep the majority of our players together through this three-year cycle, leading into another mega auction next year. So we've decided to release six players going into the IPL (2027) and have retained 19," Ponting told JioStar.Explaining the value Pandya brings to the side, Ponting said: "We've obviously brought in, through trade, Hardik Pandya, and traded out Arshdeep Singh. We've got a very well-rounded squad. Obviously, there's been a lot of talk about how many all-rounders we've got in our group."With Hardik coming in and Marco Jansen, Marcus Stoinis, Azmatullah (Omarzai), (Suryansh) Shedge, Shashank (Singh), Cooper Connolly, there are a lot of all-rounders there."It will hold us in really good stead. We've got a lot of bases covered there as far as spin bowling all-rounders and fast bowling all-rounders are concerned," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A suffered early setbacks in their opening match of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 as both explosive openers, Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, fell cheaply against Nepal in Doha.The highly rated batting duo failed to make the most of their starts as Nepal's bowlers exploited a tricky surface to put the Indian side on the back foot.After Nepal elected to bowl first, Abhishek and Sooryavanshi began cautiously, with the pitch offering assistance to the bowlers.The ball held up on the surface, making stroke-making difficult and preventing the Indian openers from playing their natural attacking game.Abhishek managed nine runs off 13 deliveries, including a six, before Nandan Yadav provided Nepal with the first breakthrough in the sixth over. Looking to play a big shot, the left-hander swung early at a full delivery but got it off the toe-end of his bat.The ball went high towards mid-on, where substitute fielder Abhishesh Gautam took a comfortable catch.Sooryavanshi initially looked more fluent, showing glimpses of his attacking ability with three boundaries and a six. He scored 26 off 32 deliveries but failed to convert his start into a substantial score.Pawan Sarraf eventually dismissed the young opener in the 11th over. Sooryavanshi attempted to clear his front leg and launch a delivery down the ground, but the ball gripped the surface and turned past his bat to hit the top of middle stump.The dismissals left India A under pressure, with Nepal making good use of the conditions. Ayush Badoni also fell for just two after being stumped off Lalit Rajbanshi, leaving India A three wickets down inside 11 overs.With the top order back in the pavilion, the responsibility shifted to captain Tilak Varma and the middle order to rebuild the innings and guide India A towards a competitive total.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aiden Markram to captain South Africa in second Test against Bangladesh as Temba Bavuma ruled out
articles.summary: South Africa will have a change in leadership for the second and final Test against Bangladesh, with Aiden Markram set to captain the side in place of
articles.body: South Africa will have a change in leadership for the second and final Test against Bangladesh, with Aiden Markram set to captain the side in place of injured Temba Bavuma. Cricket South Africa (CSA) confirmed on Thursday that Bavuma has been ruled out of the series finale due to a right calf strain sustained during the opening Test at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg.Bavuma's absence comes after South Africa registered a comprehensive nine-wicket victory in the first Test to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series. The Proteas will now look to complete a series whitewash under Markram when the second Test gets underway at SuperSport Park in Centurion on November 23.All-rounder Senuran Muthusamy has been added to the South African squad as Bavuma's replacement, while Markram will take over the captaincy responsibilities for the final encounter.Temba Bavuma ruled out after calf injuryBavuma sustained the injury while batting in South Africa's first innings of the opening Test. The Proteas captain initially retired hurt on 49 but returned to the crease the following day to complete an impressive unbeaten 68. However, the 36-year-old did not take the field during Bangladesh's second innings as South Africa completed their nine-wicket victory on the fifth day.Bavuma confirmed after the match that he would miss the second Test and begin rehabilitation under the supervision of the team's medical staff. His availability for the upcoming white-ball assignments against Bangladesh remains uncertain. The injury is another setback for the South African skipper, who has dealt with several fitness issues during his international career.Aiden Markram takes charge as South Africa eye series sweepMarkram will now lead the Proteas in the series finale as they look to maintain their winning momentum. The opener has previously captained South Africa in international cricket and brings considerable leadership experience to the side.Bavuma's absence also leaves a vacancy in the middle order. Tony de Zorzi, who is already part of the squad, is among the options to replace the regular captain in the playing XI. South Africa will take confidence from their performance in the opening Test, where they recovered after Bangladesh posted 400 in their first innings.The hosts responded with 557, powered by debutant Marques Ackerman's 157 and contributions from the middle order. Simon Harmer then produced a match-winning spell of 6/51 to dismiss Bangladesh for 168 in their second innings, setting up a modest target that South Africa chased down with nine wickets in hand.The second Test in Centurion, scheduled from November 23 to 27, will give Markram an opportunity to guide South Africa to a 2-0 series victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
